og_title: BJJ Strength Training: Programming for Grapplers
description: Strength training programming for BJJ practitioners. Compound lifts, sport-specific exercises, weekly programming, and recovery.
intro_paragraphs: Strength training amplifies your BJJ — but bad programming can drain mat performance.
The goal is functional strength that supports grappling: posterior chain, grip, and neck.

sections.heading: Why Strength Matters for BJJ
items: Stronger athletes maintain frames longer, finish submissions cleaner, and resist position breaks.
Strength is a force multiplier on top of technical skill — but never a substitute.

items.text: Squat, deadlift, pull-up, push press cover 80% of the value.
More than 2 sessions cuts into BJJ recovery.
5x5 or 3x5 for strength. Avoid endurance ranges.
More is not better. Recovery is when growth happens.

faq.question: Should I lift before or after BJJ?
faq.answer: After if same day, or on different days. Lifting before BJJ depletes glycogen and reduces technical performance.

faq.question: Do I need to bulk to get stronger?
faq.answer: Not for relative strength. Many BJJ athletes maintain weight while increasing strength via skill development.
